study_design: Hospital-based case-control study of incident, histologically confirmed prostate cancer.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Cases were 1 294 men with incident, histologically confirmed prostate cancer, admitted to the major teaching and general hospitals of five Italian areas between 1991 and 2002. Controls were 1 451 men admitted for acute, non-neoplastic conditions to the same hospitals.
reason: The abstract evaluates incident prostate cancer overall and does not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Vitamin E showed a significant inverse association with prostate cancer (OR = 0.78 for the highest versus the lowest tertile of intake, 95% CI: 0.58-0.96; p-value for trend = 0.02), whereas for vitamin C the inverse association was of borderline statistical significance (OR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.65-1.08).
estimate_classifications.reason: The vitamin E estimate is for overall incident prostate cancer, with no aggressive endpoint specified.
